text:
San Jose beat Los Angeles 5-4 in overtime, and the Kings had the better of the game by a wide margin. By expected goals, the quality of chances, LAK led 3.87 to 1.85, and in simulated replays of every shot they win this game 81 percent of the time. They outattempted the Sharks 69 to 47 and generated more danger in every period, including 1.43 to 0.52 in the third. What decided it was how little San Jose needed to score. Kiefer Sherwood's snap shot in the second carried a 1 percent chance of going in, Nolan Allan's wrister was a 5 percent look, and Igor Chernyshov's backhand early in the third was 6 percent.

Those three goals turned a 1-0 Kings lead into a 4-2 Sharks edge. Anton Forsberg faced chances worth 1.85 expected goals and allowed five, about three more than an average goalie would have, while Yaroslav Askarov was close to par against 3.87 expected goals and stopped 31 of 35. Los Angeles never stopped pushing. Quinton Byfield scored on a power play with two seconds left in the second, Erik Haula tipped one in at 10:21 of the third, and Artemi Panarin tied it with a slap shot at 15:00.

Overtime was the one stretch San Jose controlled, 0.29 expected goals to 0.16, and Chernyshov finished it at 3:18 with a slap shot off a Macklin Celebrini pass. It was his second goal, and he took first star with a goal-and-assist night in 16 minutes. Tyler Toffoli added a goal and an assist, and the Sharks got a power-play goal from him early in the second. Adrian Kempe took six shots and 1.19 individual expected goals for the Kings, and he came away with one goal and a loss.
